account: The MASAI trial randomized 105,934 women screened at four sites in southwest Sweden (Malmö, Lund, Landskrona and Trelleborg) between 12 April 2021 and 7 December 2022. In the intervention arm, Transpara version 1.7.0 scored each examination, and the score decided whether one or two radiologists read it. The software also marked suspicious findings. The control arm used standard double reading without AI. The AI arm needed 61,248 screen readings against 109,692 in the control arm, a 44.2% reduction in workload. Cancer detection was 6.4 per 1,000 women with AI support and 5.0 per 1,000 without, with more small node-negative invasive cancers found. A later analysis found that the interval cancer rate with AI was non-inferior and that sensitivity was higher (80.5% against 73.8%), with equal specificity. Lund University researchers led the trial with funding from the Swedish Cancer Society and Swedish government research funds.

ai_role.statement: Women were randomized by the picture archive system to AI-supported reading or standard double reading, so the trial isolates the AI-supported protocol. The protocol combines triage with detection marks, and the trial does not separate the two.
